sources.title: G4400 Modbus parameter list (Address Register CSV)
sources.note: Parameter code, size, read/write, type and the FC3 and FC4 register addresses.

sources.title: How to Read and Write MODBUS Parameters for Device Series
sources.note: Explains the address columns, function codes, default slave address and write procedure.

notes: Modbus RTU (default 19200 baud) or Modbus TCP (default port 502); the default slave address is 159. The device accepts up to three concurrent Modbus TCP users on consecutive ports.

The manufacturer's list gives each parameter two addresses: an FC3 column counted in 32-bit registers and an FC4 column counted in 16-bit registers. Only the FC4 addresses are used here. The manual says to read with function 04 and to enter the table address minus the 30001 offset, so the addresses are the wire addresses (address base 0). Read-only parameters are input registers; writable parameters (written with functions 06 and 16 after writing the authentication code to register 998) are listed as holding registers at the same address.

Float and 32-bit values take two 16-bit registers, 64-bit values four. The byte and word order are not stated; big-endian with the high word first is assumed. Integer signedness is not stated; unsigned is assumed. 'File time' values are 8-byte timestamps.
Parameter names are the manufacturer's parameter codes without the PRM_CODE_ prefix; the list gives no units or descriptions, so none are added.

Left out: parameters whose type the list marks UNKNOWN, action commands, integer parameters whose size and type columns disagree, strings of size 0, and the harmonic, interharmonic and spectrum vector registers, which need a selector register written first (see the manufacturer's guide, section 5). Unused registers inside large blocks read as NaN (0xFFFFFFFF).
Written from the manufacturer's manual; not tested on a device.
